findings.title: No code computes the Hypervolume (diversity) metric reported in every table
findings.claim: calc_all_metrics() enumerates every metric the evaluation produces (full key set: coverage, validity, actionability, sparsity, proximity_continuous_manhattan, proximity_continuous_euclidean, prob_plausibility, log_density_cf/test, lof_scores_cf/test, isolation_forest_scores_cf/test); a repo-wide grep for hypervolume/pymoo/pygmo/HV returns zero non-comment hits.
findings.concern: Diversity — measured by Hypervolume — is a headline claim in the abstract and a column in Tables 1, 3, 6 and 8, yet no code in the repository computes it, so the reported diversity numbers cannot be reproduced or checked.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add the hypervolume computation used to fill the Hypervol. columns (library, reference point, and objective axes), or point to where it lives.
findings.reason: Quote matches metrics.py lines 359-363 exactly; check_traceability.py confirms zero non-comment hypervolume/pymoo/pygmo/HV hits across all .py files.

findings.title: No implementation of any baseline (DiCE, CCHVAE, ReViSE, TABCF, Wachter)
findings.claim: The only documented reproduction command trains and evaluates DiCoFlex alone; a whole-word repo grep for cchvae/dice/revise/tabcf/wachter/carla finds zero non-comment hits, and there is no baseline module, wrapper, or CARLA-style dependency in the tree.
findings.concern: Table 1's central comparison (and Fig 2's runtime comparison) is against five baseline methods whose code is entirely absent, so the headline 'outperforms existing methods' claim cannot be reproduced from this repository.
findings.resolution: Authors: please provide the baseline configurations/wrappers (or the exact external commands + versions) used to generate the CCHVAE/DiCE/ReViSE/TABCF/Wachter rows of Table 1.
findings.reason: README.md line 68 quote confirmed; check_traceability.py reports zero whole-word baseline hits (cchvae/dice/revise/tabcf/wachter/carla) in all .py files; .gitignore has 'results_dice/*' but no implementation.

findings.title: Table 1 'Classif. prob.' column has no producing code
findings.quote:
X = self.X_cf if cf else self.X_test
X = torch.from_numpy(X).float()
y = torch.from_numpy(self.y_target).float()
gen_log_probs = self.gen_model(X, y).detach().numpy()
return (gen_log_probs > self.prob_plausibility_threshold).mean()
findings.claim: The only probability-named metric, prob_plausibility(), thresholds the generative flow's log-density; no metric queries the discriminator's confidence in the target class (disc_model.predict_proba), and calc_all_metrics() returns no such key.
findings.concern: Every row of Table 1 reports a 'Classif. prob.' (model confidence in the target prediction), but the evaluation code computes no classifier-confidence metric, so that column is not traceable.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add or point to the code that computes the per-counterfactual target-class probability aggregated into the Classif. prob. column.
findings.reason: Quote at metrics.py lines 205-209 confirmed; check_traceability.py AST walk of calc_all_metrics() returns no classifier-confidence key; disc_model.predict_proba appears only in commented-out lines 738-739.

findings.title: The four actionability masks of Tables 2/6 are not defined anywhere
findings.quote:
features = dataset.X_train.shape[1]
masks = []
masks.append(np.ones(features) * 1e-3)
masks = np.array(masks)

mask_features = len(masks)
print(masks)
findings.claim: The driver constructs exactly one mask — a uniform 1e-3 weight vector that protects no feature — so the actionability mechanism is never exercised on any specific feature in the committed configuration.
findings.concern: Tables 2 and 6 report DiCoFlex trained with four masks blocking Capital Gain, Capital Loss, Age, Race/Sex, and Native Country, but those mask patterns exist nowhere in the code, so the actionability experiments cannot be reproduced as run.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add the mask definitions (which feature indices each of masks 1-4 protects, and the α penalty value) used for Tables 2 and 6.
findings.reason: Quote at train_generic_counterfactual.py lines 152-158 confirmed exactly; only one uniform mask (all features weighted 1e-3) is constructed; no feature-specific masks for Tables 2/6 exist anywhere in the repo.

findings.title: Driver appends two hardcoded absolute sys.path entries from authors' machines
findings.claim: The main entry point unconditionally appends a Windows path under a specific user's home and a Linux path under another user's home to sys.path.
findings.concern: These are dead machine-specific paths (harmless no-ops on any other host since the package is installed via setup.py, but they signal the script was run ad hoc and leak author usernames); they should be removed for a clean release.
findings.resolution: Remove the two sys.path.append lines and rely on the installed package / PYTHONPATH.
findings.reason: Both sys.path.append lines confirmed at lines 5-6 of train_generic_counterfactual.py, verbatim match.

findings.title: The 'MaskedAutoregressiveFlow' used everywhere is built from SimpleRealNVP, not MAF
findings.quote:
model = _SimpleRealNVP(
    features=features,
    hidden_features=hidden_features,
    context_features=context_features,
    num_layers=num_layers,
    num_blocks_per_layer=num_blocks_per_layer,
    activation=activation,
    use_volume_preserving=False,
    dropout_probability=dropout_probability,
    batch_norm_within_layers=batch_norm_within_layers,
    batch_norm_between_layers=batch_norm_between_layers,
)
findings.claim: The class named MaskedAutoregressiveFlow instantiates nflows' SimpleRealNVP (affine coupling / RealNVP) and takes model._transform as its transform; the imported MaskedAffineAutoregressiveTransform is never used (0 uses outside the import, verified by AST). The driver uses this class for both the plausibility model (train_...py:75) and the counterfactual flow (train_...py:184).
findings.concern: The paper states in §3.2 that MAF was selected as the flow, and Appendix D / Table 5 justifies this with an NLL ablation where MAF (−43.30) beats RealNVP (26.58); but the released model is RealNVP, so the stated architecture is wrong, the model-selection ablation is not reproducible, and all main results were produced by a different (per the paper's own Table 5, worse-NLL) flow than claimed.
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm whether experiments used MAF or RealNVP; if RealNVP, correct §3.2/Appendix D and Table 5, or release the actual MAF (stacked MaskedAffineAutoregressiveTransform) code used for the reported numbers.
findings.reason: Quote at maf.py lines 130-141 confirmed; check_traceability.py AST confirms MaskedAffineAutoregressiveTransform has zero non-import uses and exactly 1 _SimpleRealNVP() construction; class is named MaskedAutoregressiveFlow (line 109).

findings.title: ε-sparsity implemented as absolute threshold over all features, not Eq 30's relative change over continuous features
findings.claim: calc_all_metrics() calls sparsity(eps=0.05), which flags a feature as changed when the absolute difference |x_test − x_cf| exceeds 0.05, averaged over ALL features (continuous and one-hot categorical); there is no division by |x| and no continuous/categorical split.
findings.concern: Paper Eq 30 defines ε-sparsity as a RELATIVE change I(|x−x'|/|x| > ε) averaged over continuous features only, and Eq 29 defines categorical sparsity separately; the single absolute all-feature metric matches neither Table 1 sparsity column, so those columns are not computed as defined (the code's version is a valid-ish proxy, hence 'difference', but it is ambiguous whether this exact function produced the table).
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm which function produced the 'Sparsity cat.' and 'ε-sparsity cont.' columns; if it is this one, reconcile the absolute-vs-relative and all-features-vs-continuous discrepancies with Eq 29/30.
findings.reason: Quote at metrics.py lines 187-193 confirmed; check_traceability.py confirms absolute diff (no relative normalization by X_test), covering all features with no categorical/continuous split.

findings.title: Adult loader subsamples to 2,000 rows; paper reports 32,000
findings.claim: AdultDataset.preprocess() randomly draws 2,000 rows (with no random_state) from each of the train and test CSVs before any modelling.
findings.concern: Table 4 reports Adult Census = 32,000 samples 'used for our experiments', but the code uses 2,000; Adult is also the dataset behind Tables 2, 3, 5 and 6, so those ablations run on 2,000 non-deterministically-sampled rows rather than the stated size.
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm the actual sample size used for the Adult experiments and either fix the loader or correct Table 4; add a random_state for reproducibility.
findings.reason: Quote at adult.py lines 80-81 confirmed; check_traceability.py reports raw_data.sample(2000) with no random_state, contradicting Table 4's stated 32,000 samples.
